caption: Figure 3. An example that maps a MatMul operator to two cores with the compute-shift style execution. Both (b) and (c) are valid compute-shift execution plans, but with different tradeoffs between memory footprint and communication overhead.
subject: how a MatMul operator can be partitioned across 2 cores either spatially only, or also temporally into 2 shift steps

groups.why_chosen: One coloured Input/Weight/Output key from the whole-matrix panel is reused unchanged through both partition variants, and a nested Step/Shift/Step insert shows the exact tiles trading places.
groups.what_to_learn: Fix one colour per Input row-block, Weight column-block and Output block in the whole-operator panel, reuse those exact colours in every partitioned variant, and show the trade as a half-filled output block that a Shift sub-frame completes.
